title: Stability Sync-up: Ops Lab Playbook & 30/60/90 Sprint Journal
content:
Purpose
This working doc captures a compact, pragmatic plan to run a cross-functional "Ops Lab" that accelerates SLO adoption across feature teams, validates reliability tactics in a controlled sprint cadence, and produces repeatable handoffs for long-term SLA/SLO management. The goal is to run three 30/60/90 day waves (fast experiments -> stabilize -> scale) and produce a checklist, signal map, and a set of roll/rollback recipes that product and infra teams can reuse.

Context & why now
- Several product launches this quarter increase tail-latency risk for the hosted inference API.
- Platform metrics show a 12% increase in 95th-percentile token generation latency over baseline in EU-region during peak.
- Teams are asking for concrete SLO templates and low-effort experiments that prove improvement without blocking feature delivery.

High-level approach
- Ops Lab = small cross-functional pod that pairs SRE + product engineer + infra operator + data analyst. Run three waves: 30d exploratory, 60d stabilization, 90d scale/hand-off.
- Emphasize cheap, observable experiments: traffic shaping, KV-cache priming, ephemeral batching config, aggressive prefix caching, model-variant fallbacks.
- Record experiments as tiny reproducible runbooks with inputs, metrics, expected signal changes, and rollback criteria.

Success metrics (primary)
- 95th percentile per-route latency reduced by >= 15% for targeted routes in production traffic within the 60-day wave.
- Error budget burn rate under 0.5x during 90-day stabilization window for the service group.
- Teams adopt at least one standardized SLO template and automated alert runbook by handoff.

Secondary outcomes
- Reduction in token-unit cost for guarded traffic via batching/caching experiments (target: 5% unit cost reduction).
- Clear dependency map and ownership matrix for long-running reliability work.

Ops Lab cadence & artifacts
- Weekly sync (30m) with pod to review signals and blockers.
- Bi-weekly stakeholder demo (30-45m) for product, infra, and Console team.
- Deliverables: experiment runbook (one per experiment), metrics dashboard (per-route token/latency/error), rollout recipe, final handoff pack.

Roles & responsibilities (example pod)
- Pod lead (SRE): Asha Patel — runbook owner, escalation contact, oncall alignment.
- Product engineer: Miguel Torres — implements traffic shaping and client-side fallback logic for canary.
- Infra operator: Liang Chen — implements batching/caching changes and measures cost.
- Data analyst: Priya Nair — signal extraction, dashboards, statistical checks.
- QA/owner for rollouts: Samir Gupta — gate criteria and rollback triggers for canary.

30/60/90 wave plan (practical checklist)
- 0-7 days (kickoff + discovery)
  - Inventory routes and existing SLOs. Quick signal hygiene: ensure 1m resolution traces, 95/99 latency buckets, and synthetic checks exist.
  - Run tabletop: failure modes for the sprint and identify top-3 quick experiments.
  - Create canary traffic harness (sandbox) and dev-account flags.
- 8-30 days (fast experiment window)
  - Run 3 small experiments in parallel (each needs a runbook): e.g., prefix-KV cache priming, adjusted batching window, and model-variant downgrade under load.
  - Measure immediate signal delta and update the dashboard. Tag experiments as "promising" or "discard" after statistical check.
  - Document quick wins as change requests for 60d wave.
- 31-60 days (stabilize & iterate)
  - Promote 1–2 promising experiments to gradual canary in production with clear rollback triggers.
  - Set SLO guardrails and automated alerts on error budget burn and latency slope.
  - Run mid-wave retrospective, update runbooks, start drafting handoff pack.
- 61-90 days (scale & handoff)
  - Finalize automated deployment of winning config (templates for Redwood Console and infra-as-code).
  - Training session for product teams on the SLO template and runbook usage.
  - Handoff: create tickets for long-term platform work and mark owners.

Experiment runbook template (minimum fields)
- Title, author, date, brief description
- Hypothesis (what we expect to change and why)
- Input parameters (traffic %, batching/window size, cache TTL, model variant)
- Measurement plan (metrics, dashboards, alert thresholds, compare windows)
- Rollout plan (staged percentages, duration per stage)
- Rollback criteria (explicit signal thresholds and commands)
- Postmortem template link

Communication plan
- Slack: #ops-lab-stability for live updates and quick blockers. Post experiment start + end + result.
- Bi-weekly demos recorded and uploaded to Confluence (linked_artifacts).
- Critical alerts go to SRE pager on-call and the product stakeholder distribution list (email + slack).

Decision points & gating
- Gate 1 (end of 30d): choose experiments to promote based on at least two independent metric improvements and no increased error budget burn.
- Gate 2 (end of 60d): production canary approved for scale if rollback works and cost delta < 10% increase (unless stakeholder approves otherwise).
- Gate 3 (handoff): product team owns day-to-day SLO, platform owns automation and console integration.

Risks & mitigations (quick list)
- Risk: experiment causes silent correctness regressions. Mitigation: pair metric checks with sample-based output regression tests and lightweight eval prompt sets.
- Risk: increased cost from aggressive caching or replication. Mitigation: cost-monitoring dashboards and budget alert thresholds.
- Risk: ownership confusion post-handoff. Mitigation: documented SLA matrix and scheduled 30/60 day post-handoff check-ins.

Template SLOs for teams (examples to adapt)
- Product-facing text-generation route: 99th token generation latency < 1.8s, target availability 99.95% monthly, error budget 0.05%
- Internal admin route: 95th latency < 300ms, lower priority on cost.

Quick experiments (examples to run in 30d)
- KV cache priming: pro-actively fill prefix cache for top 20 queries; measure 95p latency improvement and cache hit rate.
- Batching shape test: reduce batching window from 50ms -> 20ms for low-latency routes and compare unit cost.
- Model variant fallback: route long tails to a faster quantized variant when predicted sequence length > X. Observe response quality via spot checks.

Weekly note template (pod use)
- Date, experiment status, key metric deltas, blockers, next steps, owner for next action.

Handoff pack checklist
- Final dashboard link + baseline comparisons
- Experiment runbooks and postmortems
- SLO template and alert rules (Console snippet)
- IAM/ownership matrix and escalation points
- Quickstart: how to re-run the experiment locally or in staging (dev flags, commands)

Immediate next steps (this doc action list)
- [ ] Finalize pod members and schedule kickoff (owner: Asha; due: 2026-06-18)
- [ ] Provision sandbox canary org & synthetic checks (owner: Liang; due: 2026-06-20)
- [ ] Draft first 3 runbooks with clear measurement plans (owner: Miguel; due: 2026-06-22)
- [ ] Create shared dashboard and link to Confluence (owner: Priya; due: 2026-06-24)

Notes to self / running log (raw, informal)
- 2026-06-15: Kickoff — product teams willing to try conservative batching change. Need to confirm cost SLA with finance for potential short-term spike.
- 2026-06-18: Miguel started KV priming PoC in staging; initial hit rate looks promising (30% hit on top-10 queries).
- 2026-06-25: First canary attempt revealed increased 99p for a corner case; paused and filed a deep-dive (ENG-1379).

Appendix: useful checks and quick commands
- How to compare canary vs baseline in dashboard: set compare windows to prior 24h and use p95/p99 and token count normalized by traffic.
- Rollback one-liner (example): curl -X POST https://api.redwood-internal/release/rollback -d '{"service":"api-gen","tag":"pre-kv"}' (replace with staging-safe script in runbook).

End of doc — this is intentionally concise and operational. Iterate runbooks aggressively; the highest value is reproducible, safe, low-friction changes product teams will actually enable.
